speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient is an 8-year-old girl with a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain following amoxicillin treatment for sinusitis. The rash started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae and spread to the trunk and extremities. Given the timing (one week after starting antibiotics) and the nature of the symptoms (itchy rash, joint pain, fever), this presentation is highly consistent with Serum Sickness-Like Reaction (SSLR), a common adverse reaction to antibiotics like amoxicillin or cefaclor in children. The normal urinalysis and abdominal ultrasound help rule out IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein Purpura) which typically presents with palpable purpura and often involves the kidneys or GI tract. The "itchy" nature of the rash favors SSLR over the non-itchy purpura of HSP.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum Sickness-Like Reaction
